papers.title: Recovery Budgets for Persistent AI-Agent Memory: Reproducibility Artifact
papers.summary: Complete computational-reproduction artifact associated with Recovery Budgets for Persistent AI-Agent Memory: Bounding Revocation Liability. Includes original structural and recorded Codex/Claude workflows, a separately frozen extension over 120 held-out full-history LongMemEval-derived questions, two Claude API models, two repetitions and seven policies (3360 paired policy executions), complete public benchmark input, exact requests/responses and usage, durable SQLite stores, seven preserved infrastructure refusals, exploratory controls, runtime tests, statistical analysis and figure/table generators. Offline reproduction uses recorded responses and requires no API key or model charge. It does not constitute independent new model sampling. Weighted-pending quotas and reservations intentionally agree; episodic memory remains competitive. Scores are strict short-reference EM/F1 rather than official LongMemEval scores. Direct study-author identifiers are withheld in this review artifact; third-party data attribution is retained. See README.txt, DATA-DICTIONARY.txt, ANONYMIZATION.txt, and verification reports for scope and limitations. Licenses: MIT applies to original software; CC BY 4.0 applies to original experimental outputs and documentation. LongMemEval material retains its original MIT notice and attribution. papers.title: Design and evaluation of an agent-based digital-twin-inspired simulation for metacognition research in higher education
papers.summary: Background There is a significant gap between sophisticated models of metacognition and empirical testing of these models in educational settings, especially the hierarchical AMERT model. Agent-based simulation frameworks, and their conceptual evolution toward simulation-based digital twins, remain largely underutilized in higher education as virtual laboratories for hypothesis generation, despite their potential to model complex developmental dynamics. Objective This study aimed to design and internally evaluate a simulation-based digital twin framework that combines the five-level AMERT model and agent-based architecture to investigate the dynamics of metacognitive development. Method Using Design and Development Research (DDR), we developed the framework through theoretical synthesis and subjected its conceptual content to expert review via a modified Delphi method with 12 experts. Student agents were simulated using NetLogo and represented four computational learner archetypes. Instructional scenarios were simulated for 150 ticks and repeated 50 times for each scenario, and internal consistency of the simulation logic was examined using Graph Neural Networks; the outputs remained systematically distinguishable across the predefined computational archetypes (89% classification accuracy). papers.title: Knowledge Graphs as External Memory for LLM-based Scientific Assistants
papers.summary: Scientific assistants must remember the questions, observations, parameters, and intermediate results that accumulate across days or weeks of inquiry, and trace each conclusion back to its evidence. Large Language Models (LLMs) lack such a structured, persistent memory, which causes contextual degradation, hallucinations, and excessive cost from overusing the context window. This thesis proposes a neuro-symbolic architecture that couples an LLM-based agent with a knowledge graph (KG) built on standardized formal languages (RDF, RDFS, OWL 2 RL, SHACL, SPARQL) and reusing existing ontologies (e.g. PROV-O) whenever possible. In contrast to state-of-the-art memory systems, which rely on schemaless or proprietary property graphs, our hypothesis is that grounding agent memory in open standards improves the six memory operations (consolidation, indexing, updating, forgetting, retrieval, compression) through formal reasoning and declarative validation, at a latency overhead that stays negligible relative to the LLM call. We present the problem, three research questions and their hypotheses, a first experimental prototype that implements an end-to-end store-and-retrieve pipeline, and an evaluation plan combining the LongMemEval and LoCoMo benchmarks with a test case in metabolomics.

papers.title: STRATUM: Repository Memory for Coding Agents — Replication Package
papers.summary: Anonymous replication package for a double-blind submission arguing that coding agents need persistent, experience-aware repository memory rather than a larger context window. Contains every script and raw measurement behind the paper's motivating study and preliminary experiments: F1 — token census of six open-source repositories and the representation-cost gap between storing knowledge as indexed text vs. as model key-value (KV) cache state (e.g. ~4 GB as text vs. ~298 TB as fp16 KV state per billion tokens, 70B model). F2 — the working-set size of 752 real bug-fix commits: the median fix touches two files, and the one-hop import closure is 2.7-9.9% of the repository. F3 — how much of real file co-change is visible to static analysis (852 commits, 4 repositories): 47.3% of co-edited file pairs remain disconnected even under transitive import reachability and test-name links. E4 — retrieval latency over a synthetic 10^6-node SQLite+HNSW store: 1.70 ms median / 2.76 ms p99 end-to-end. E5 — a real multi-session agent experiment on 8 real bugs using the Claude API: a reader model that inherits a different (writer) model's memory diagnoses the bug correctly in 21/24 trials vs. 6/24 for a retrieval-only baseline (one-sided Fisher exact p = 1.27e-05), at 4.5x lower median token cost; accumulated memory (26 pooled notes) stays at 8/8; a whole-repository-in-context baseline matches me

papers.title: Intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding for STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning: a multi-dimensional framework and empirical evaluation
papers.summary: STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning (PBL) asks students to knit together knowledge their courses have kept apart, and to do so while absorbing the ordinary friction of group work. Scaffolding designed for single-discipline tasks rarely keeps pace with either demand. This paper proposes an intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding model comprising four architectural layers—data perception, intelligent analysis, strategy decision, and interaction execution—supported by three specialized functional agents targeting cognitive guidance, process coordination, and reflection facilitation. A multi-dimensional feature fusion approach employing scaled dot-product attention diagnoses collaborative states in near real time, reaching a macro-averaged $$\:{F}_{1}$$ of 0.83 on a test set split by team, and a timing policy trained with Proximal Policy Optimization decides when to intervene while a fading rule decides when to withdraw. Twenty-four five-member teams (120 undergraduates) completed two interdisciplinary projects over six weeks under agent-based scaffolding, teacher-led scaffolding, or unsupported collaboration. Because students were nested in teams and several outcomes are defined at team level, condition effects were estimated with baseline-adjusted, cluster-robust models rather than treating the 120 students as independent. papers.title: Agentic AI for Complex Decision-Making: A Systematic Critical Review of Planning, Memory, Tools, Safety and Assurance in Autonomous Systems
The End of Consensus Research?
papers.summary: Consensus is a fundamental problem in distributed computing and at the core of state machine replication (SMR). Despite decades of active human research, discovering practical low-latency solutions to the problem is still open, as it requires combining protocol knowledge, correctness reasoning, implementation, and experimental evaluation. We report on how AI helped us discover A-greement, a new consensus protocol for geo-replicated state machines that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art solutions. Averaged across six deployments with 5 or 9 replicas, A-greement reduces the mean latency of a geo-distributed key-value store over the fastest baseline by 12.2% and 33.3% on write-heavy and read-heavy workloads, respectively, and matches the fastest baseline on read-only workloads. A-greement combines lease-authorized local reads, direct client learning for leader-ordered writes, and a fast fixed-quorum per-key write path, selected according to network topology and workload. At the heart of our discovery lies AI-greement, an agent harness for the "autonomous" discovery, implementation, experimentation, and verification of candidate protocols. AI-greement integrates (1) a concept-oriented protocol knowledge base, (2) a modular implementation skeleton, and (3) a Lean-based verification framework with reusable safety definitions, reference specifications, and proofs. papers.title: Design and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Predicting Twelfth-Grade Students’ Mathematics Performance Based on Individual, Educational, and Learning Technology Factors
papers.summary: Purpose: This study aimed to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence–based model for predicting the mathematics performance of twelfth-grade experimental sciences students based on individual, educational, and learning technology factors. Methods and Materials: This applied, quantitative, cross-sectional, and predictive study was conducted among twelfth-grade experimental sciences students in Isfahan, Iran. A total of 187 questionnaires were distributed, and after removing incomplete, inconsistent, and invalid records, data from 84 students were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing individual factors, educational conditions, and learning technology variables, together with students’ recorded mathematics scores. The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets, and repeated five-fold cross-validation was used for internal model development. Multiple linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, elastic net regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, and support vector regression were compared. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and the coefficient of determination. Findings: Previous mathematics achievement had the strongest positive correlation with current mathematics performance, followed by mathematics se

papers.title: Governing Agentic AI in Africa: A Systematic Literature Review of Ethical Challenges, Framework Gaps, and Ubuntu-Informed Governance Solutions
papers.summary: Agentic AI systems pursue goals through multi-step planning, tool use, memory, and adaptive action, creating governance challenges that differ from those associated with conventional predictive or generative AI. This study systematically reviews governance evidence relevant to agentic AI in Africa and develops an Ubuntu-informed conceptual framework. Following PRISMA 2020, 91 records published from 2019 to April 2026 were analysed through quantitative content analysis and abductive thematic synthesis. The corpus comprises 12 agentic-AI-specific records, 3 agentic-adjacent records, and 76 broader AI-governance records used as contextual evidence. Five literature-derived gaps were identified: accountability across autonomous action chains, infrastructure-aware oversight, bias and representational harm, policy fragmentation, and community exclusion. These findings inform five proposed governance elements: communal impact assessment, collective consent and participation, infrastructure-contingent oversight, African dataset and bias auditing, and communal accountability. The framework is a literature-derived conceptual proposition, not an empirically validated governance instrument, and requires future case-study, expert-panel, and comparative policy testing.

papers.title: Agent-based simulation of equity-oriented water reallocation under drought: A case study of the Geum River Basin
papers.summary: Study region : Geum River Basin, South Korea, a structurally heterogeneous watershed with 14 agricultural, 12 domestic/industrial intake, and 3 hydropower stakeholders. The basin has the highest agricultural water demand among South Korea’s six major river basins, with precipitation concentrated in the summer monsoon season, making dam operations critical for balancing competing water demands during irrigation. Study focus : This study develops an integrated framework to improve equitable water allocation during droughts by coupling a basin-scale allocation model with an Agent-Based Model (ABM). While centralized optimization overlooks decentralized social dynamics, autonomous stakeholder agents make voluntary diversion decisions based on locally perceived reliability deficits, redistributing water to the most vulnerable peers via hypothetical conveyance infrastructure. Streamflow is represented by SWAT-derived daily inflows spanning 39 water years (October 1981–September 2020). New hydrological insights and conclusions : First, agricultural water supply vulnerability in the Geum River Basin is governed less by absolute demand magnitude and more by basin topology and infrastructure configuration. papers.title: Large Language Model Adoption and Firm Innovation: More Patents within Existing Knowledge Boundaries
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) let employees search, explain, and recombine technical knowledge at low cost. We ask whether firms that adopt them innovate more and whether they innovate beyond the technologies they already know. Using a classifier validated against human coders, we date when Chinese listed firms first confirm, in replies to investor questions, that they have put LLMs or other AI applications into use, and we link these events to the patent applications of 1,836 firms over 2019--2024. Patent applications rise by 12.5% after adoption. In a second design based on the arrival of LLMs after ChatGPT's release, firms that had hired more heavily into AI-exposed occupations increased their patenting relative to other firms in 2024. The additional patents stay within firms' existing knowledge boundaries: utility-model and exploitative applications rise, new patents move closer to the firm's prior technology portfolio, and neither invention nor exploratory applications increase significantly. Adopters also raise R&D intensity, software-and-data investment, and the share of graduate employees. The patent response is concentrated in labor-intensive industries and in highly AI-exposed firms, it tilts further toward exploitation under myopic managers, and among business functions only market-facing uses are followed by significantly more patents. papers.title: Perceptions and recommendations: exploring the ethics of using satellite data to understand, monitor, and publish research on international geohazards
papers.summary: Abstract. Over the last ten years, open-access earth observation satellite data volumes have grown exponentially. Through use of this data, geohazard remote sensing scientists' abilities to impact policy and reduce societal vulnerability to geohazards has become increasingly tangible. However, much of this open-access data is acquired, stored, and disseminated by the Global North, whilst most disasters take place in the Global South. Furthermore, many societies are imaged by these earth observation satellites perhaps without knowing these satellites exist. There exists little ethical guidance for remote sensing researchers in navigating ethical risks that may arise during geohazard research which uses satellite data. We explore these ethical considerations with UK based geohazard remote sensing scientists through thirteen interviews and three focus group discussions. We discuss with scientists their thoughts on ethical review systems for geohazard remote sensing; the importance of visiting study regions; how data should be handled which images people and societies; the desired impact these scientists want to achieve; and the ethical risks of open data. We find among remote sensing researchers in industry, government organisations, and academia a deep desire to contribute to the reduction of societal vulnerabilities to geohazards. papers.title: TME LLM OS: A Closed-Loop Systems Engineering Architecture for Epistemic Correction in AI Agent Systems Systems Engineering Proposal
From Artificial Intelligence to Institutional Intelligence
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence and agentic systems can redistribute reading, research, synthesis, criticism, drafting, and coordination within courts. This article asks how that redistribution changes judicial cognition and which institutional safeguards are needed to preserve legitimate adjudication. Through an interdisciplinary narrative review and doctrinal analysis, it develops a framework of institutional intelligence anchored in Brazilian National Council of Justice Resolution No. 615/2025, as amended by Resolution No. 674/2026. Five categories organize the argument: institutional cognitive space describes the allocation of cognitive work; artificial adversariality identifies structured internal challenge among agents; the institutional rein integrates controls over delegated autonomy; meaningful human initiative emphasizes the continuing human authority to frame problems and determine purposes; and institutional AI curation describes the competence required to select, validate, contextualize, and reject artificial contributions. Recent research on human–AI collaboration and multi-agent failure qualifies the framework: neither human review nor artificial disagreement guarantees reliability, and short-term performance gains do not establish long-term professional competence. The article distinguishes technical auditability from legal reason-giving and internal agent de

papers.title: Research trends in supply chain management in the construction industry: a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis
papers.summary: Supply chain management (SCM) has become a strategic priority in construction, where project delivery depends on coordinating fragmented actors, material flows, and information under uncertainty. Despite growing scholarly attention, research remains dispersed across sustainability, digitalisation, risk governance, and stakeholder coordination, thereby limiting the development of cumulative knowledge. To address this fragmentation, this study integrates a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic literature review with bibliometric analysis to examine the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and future directions of construction SCM. A total of 143 studies (2001–2024) were identified from Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, and analysed using descriptive techniques, thematic synthesis, and bibliographic coupling in VOSviewer. The findings reveal four interrelated domains: sustainable construction SCM, strategic management and risk mitigation, digital transformation, and supplier and stakeholder management. This review provides an integrated evidence base that clarifies field fragmentation and identifies priorities for future research and practice.

papers.title: OSynth: A Longitudinal, Context-Sensitive Evaluation of Meeting Understanding
papers.summary: Meeting notetakers are increasingly deployed in settings where longitudinal context is available including calendar metadata, prior meetings, emails, slides, and speaker enrollments; however, meeting corpora remain limited in terms of size, domain coverage, and available context. We present OSynth, a large-scale synthetic dataset of simulated organizations comprising 570 hours of meeting audio together with associated artifacts and a latent ground-truth state. In a pairwise comparison, human raters distinguish OSynth meetings from real meeting transcripts with only 56% accuracy based on excerpts of 150-300 words. Across state-of-the-art LLMs, additional context yields significant gains on several entity-sensitive dimensions, demonstrating limitations of contemporary approaches and the potential usefulness of OSynth in developing better-contextualized meeting-understanding systems.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Design and Construction of a Low-Cost, Open-Source Syringe-Based Pipetting Robot Using 3D Printing and Common Hardware Parts
papers.summary: Abstract Automation in chemical laboratories improves the reproducibility, precision, and efficiency in liquid handling. A three-dimensional (3D)-printed, stepper-actuated pipetting robot was developed and tested via silver nitrate (AgNO3) experiments. The system employs a rigid 3D-printed frame to secure syringes and tubing, stepper motors for plunger actuation, and microcontroller-based software to automate the pipetting sequences. The robot was evaluated for volume accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanical reliability using 5 mL syringes. The results indicate consistent volume delivery and stable mechanical performance over multiple cycles. Detailed mechanical, electrical, and software specifications are provided to enable replication and customization in other laboratories.

papers.title: Exploring the potential of hybridized metaheuristic algorithms for photovoltaic model parameter estimation
papers.summary: Abstract Proper modeling of photovoltaic (PV) cells is a highly non-linear and multidimensional problem whose optimization using standalone meta-heuristic techniques faces premature convergence due to the large number of parameters. This paper seeks to fill in a major gap in the literature through a permutation study of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Differential Evolution (DE), Simulated Annealing (SA) and Nelder-Mead (NM) simplex method to determine the optimal "hand-off" scheme for balancing exploration and exploitation. The proposed approach has been evaluated using SDM, DDM, and TDM using R.T.C. France silicon cell, Photowatt-PWP 201 module and an independent set of data on flexible dual junction amorphous silicon cell. To ensure state-of-the-art robustness of the hybrid approach, it was also benchmarked against CEC 2017 test suite. Statistical analysis from 30 runs has been performed using Wilcoxon signed-rank test ( $$p<1.86\times {10}^{-9}$$ ), demonstrate that a sequential "Global-to-Local" transition (PSO–NM) achieves superior precision and stability, yielding a mean RMSE of $$9.32 \times 10^{ - 4}$$ for the SDM and $$1.16 \times 10^{ - 3}$$ A for the 9-parameter TDM, with coefficients of determination ( $${R}^{2}$$ ) exceeding 0.9999. Complexity analysis via the Number of Function Evaluations (NFE) shows that this hybrid method is computationally worth the effort

papers.title: Helping the Helper: LLM-Assisted Problem Articulation for Older Adults Seeking Technology Support
papers.summary: Older adults often struggle to articulate technology support needs due to unfamiliar technical terminology and age-related cognitive changes. We explore how large language models (LLMs) can facilitate this problem articulation process. Through a diary study (n = 27), we identified four communication barriers in older adults’ queries: verbosity, incompleteness, over-specification, and under-specification. To mitigate these, we developed an LLM pipeline that clarifies context and paraphrases unstructured queries. LLM-rephrased queries significantly improved automated solution accuracy (69% vs. 35%). Furthermore, younger adults (n = 48) acting as technology helpers understood LLM-rephrased queries better (93.7% vs. 65.8%) and reported greater ease in providing support. Older adults (n = 34) also found the resulting solutions highly actionable (94.7%). Finally, we contribute the first synthetic dataset of older adults’ technology assistance queries (STAQ). This work demonstrates how LLMs can improve technology support seeking for older adults by addressing age-related communication barriers.

papers.title: Chemistry-infused bandit framework for interpretable autonomous campaign of electrocatalysis
papers.summary: Abstract Autonomous experimentation offers a time-efficient route towards accelerated catalyst discovery, but current practices often rely on black-box models that are difficult to interpret. Here we demonstrate the paradigm of interpretable autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction by integrating an interpretable decision-making artificial intelligence with a fully automated electrochemical platform. Guided by a human’s chemistry-informed hypothesis, a chemistry-infused bandit is established to reflect the locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities near the explored optimum region. Not only does such a decision-making bandit lead to the discovery of previously unreported, earth-abundant electrocatalysts at least comparable to Pt-based ones, the bandit also reveals model-derived hypothesis for how synthetic conditions affect the electrocatalysts’ performance near the identified local optima as autonomous inquiry proceeds, which is otherwise untenable from black-box ones. Incorporating chemistry-informed hypothesis into the decision-making bandit is generally applicable to any chemistry problem and offers a framework for autonomous investigation, advancing hypothesis generation for catalyst’s design principles beyond simple optimization.

papers.title: SHAPING SELF-REGULATED AND METACOGNITIVE LEARNING THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND LEARNING ANALYTICS
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and learning analytics are increasingly embedded in educational systems, yet their implications for self-regulated learning (SRL) and metacognitive development remain only partially understood. This study conducts a systematic literature review of 34 empirical and review articles investigating AI-driven learning analytics in formal education settings, focusing on their impact on SRL, motivation, and academic performance. Following PRISMA-aligned procedures, the review identifies studies involving AI-based analytics tools, standardized SRL or metacognitive assessments, and empirical designs with pre–post or comparison data. The results indicate that AI-driven systems such as predictive models, adaptive platforms, chatbots, and generative AI can strengthen core SRL processes, increase motivation and engagement, and improve academic outcomes across diverse subjects and educational levels. However, the review also reveals persistent implementation challenges, including infrastructural limitations, teacher preparedness, privacy and ethical issues, and potential over-reliance on AI that may weaken independent strategic thinking. The article concludes that AI-driven learning analytics can meaningfully support SRL when embedded within coherent pedagogical frameworks and supported by institutional policies, and it outlines directions for future research on m

papers.title: Beyond Policy Engines: Binding-Complete Execution Admission
papers.summary: Policy engines determine whether evaluated policies permit a request, but a correct ALLOW decision does not establish complete governance-source participation, exact context binding, or sufficient grounds for execution admission. This paper examines the gap between policy evaluation and execution admission. We introduce the Binding-Complete Execution Admission Contract (BCEAC), a governance-relative contract for independently determined source obligations, exact policy and contextual binding, and typed admission outcomes under explicit trust assumptions. We propose a conditionally engine-agnostic architecture in which participating backends must satisfy declared semantic profiles, adapter contracts, and contextual correspondence obligations; an Execution Boundary Language (EBL) authoring syntax remains optional. The architecture separates governance resolution, policy evaluation, independent admission verification, and downstream execution mediation. We investigate two distinct experimental tracks: a finite Governance Source Completeness study and an OPA/Cedar experiment with archived native-engine records examined by offline review. The OPA/Cedar archive comprises 72 scenarios and 144 strict case-engine records (120 native-invoked and 24 pre-native), with eight additional permissive controls outside the strict denominator. The offline review did not rerun the original native O

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: Drivers of supply chain resilience in the new energy vehicle industry: An explainable machine learning approach
papers.summary: Under the global dual-carbon goals, supply chain resilience has become a strategic priority for the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry. Using a 2016–2023 panel of 403 Chinese listed NEV firms, we construct an entropy-weighted supply chain resilience index and predict it with Random Forest (RF) and XGBoost, interpreted via SHAP, against a linear regression benchmark. The tree-based ensembles explain 66%–68% of out-of-sample resilience variation, far above the linear benchmark (56%), while models using only supply chain characteristics fail to beat the sample mean. The two ensembles attribute resilience differently: transaction costs rank as the strongest supply chain predictor in RF, whereas chip import dependence dominates in XGBoost, though both agree that supply chain characteristics are stably among the top predictor groups. All five core factors exhibit nonlinear threshold patterns (on the normalized [0, 1] scale): automation first suppresses and then promotes resilience beyond a robot-penetration threshold of 0.19; government subsidies are effective mainly within an intensity window of 0.2–0.5; chip import dependence turns sharply detrimental beyond 0.77; innovation efficiency supports resilience only within an optimal moderate range, its contribution turning negative beyond 0.33; and transaction costs become resilience-enhancing only beyond thresholds of 0.15 (RF) to 0.21

papers.title: AI-assisted discrete-event simulation of public transport systems: a framework for rapid model development
papers.summary: This study presents a systematic, modular prompt-construction framework for using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist simulation modelers in public transportation systems, leveraging large language models (LLMs). By using GPT-4o and Codex, we demonstrate how discrete-event simulation (DES) executable models can be rapidly generated with our five-part prompt construction framework, requiring minimal manual coding effort. The proposed framework was tested using a real-world case study of the in-campus shuttle bus transportation system at Universitas Indonesia. The empirical data from the case study served as the foundation for constructing a simulation model that can replicate a real-world situation. This data was provided to the AI via our modular prompt-construction framework, which was then used to generate the Python code for the simulation model. The generated model results were validated based on field observation data. The generated model yielded a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 5.18%. These results indicate that LLM-assisted development of simulation models using our proposed framework can produce reliable simulation code that aligns with real-world public transportation behavior. The framework's applicability could provide a replicable, scalable method for rapid simulation development in public transportation planning and smart mobility contexts.

papers.title: Event- vs. time-driven: comparing applicability of sequential data types for machine learning-based reactive fault detection in manufacturing
papers.summary: Abstract The implementation of reliable machine learning for reactive fault detection in manufacturing requires large volumes of high-quality data. Time-series, one of the main data types in modern manufacturing, is available in high quantities, but also leads to high computational effort in model training and large number of duplicates in the data. Event-driven sequential data is another data type, used in manufacturing, reducing duplicates in data. A comparison of both sequential data types in this context is not fully explored in the literature. This paper explores a set of experiments to evaluate both sequential data types using various ML methods and windowing mechanisms on a real-world manufacturing system. Based on the results, recommendations for practitioners are derived and an outlook to possible future investigation is given.

papers.title: A Framework for Women’s Health Engineering Education: Pedagogical Foundations and Practical Implementation
papers.summary: Women represent more than half the U.S. workforce, yet women's health research and education remain systematically underprioritized, hindering technological innovation in this domain. Recent policy initiatives have elevated the profile of women's health and created urgency for engineering education to align with this shift. Despite growing recognition that advanced engineering approaches are essential to address sex-specific diseases and physiological differences, most biomedical engineering students graduate without exposure to women's health as a thematic focus or to the clinical problems and existing solutions in this space. To address this gap, we present a best practices guide based on six independently designed women's health engineering courses. Drawing on pedagogical literature and collective teaching experience, we document core elements and provide practical frameworks for both standalone women's health courses and integration into existing biomedical engineering curricula. This work is designed to lower the barrier for action, such that institutions can implement women's health engineering education scaled to their capacity and constraints. By training engineers to recognize and address systematic gaps in women's health engineering, we prepare them to build the life-changing technologies that women have long been waiting for.

papers.title: Q&A or Document-Based? The Effects of Interface Type on How Screen Reader Users Access Interconnected Documents
papers.summary: Blind and low-vision (BLV) users are increasingly engaging with large language model (LLM) interfaces to access documents, but it is unclear how such systems support or hinder their ability to build interconnected knowledge. To examine this gap, we compared a Question–Answer Interface (QAI) that supports open-ended conversational inquiry, with a Document Interface (DI) based mostly on traditional structured text document navigation. We recruited 16 BLV screen reader users where they used both interfaces to explore two fictional worlds. Data from interaction logs, concept maps, decision-based tasks, and semi-structured interviews provide comparative insights into how interface design supports knowledge construction. Findings show that participants visited more distinct documents with the DI and formed larger and more correct mental models with the DI than with the QAI. They were also more able to apply the knowledge they had gained. Simultaneously, many still preferred the QAI and often estimated that they had explored more, formed better mental models and applied their models better when acquiring the information with the QAI, despite this not being the case. Our analysis suggests possible interface design reasons for these differences and highlights some of the risks introduced by using question-answer interfaces to access information spaces.
